newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil seeks at least five pct of Tengiz.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil seeks at least five pct of Tengiz.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil is seeking at least five percent of the Tengiz oil project in Kazakhstan, LUKoil President Vagit Alekpetrov said.

LUKoil is seeking a five percent stake in the project by buying 10 percent of Chevron Corp's 50 percent share, and was also interested in an unspecified share of Kazakhstan's stake in the venture, he told journalists on a flight to Moscow from Chisinau on Wednesday.
On Tuesday Alekperov said in Chisinau that OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil was close to signing a contract to buy five percent of the Tengiz venture from Chevron.

Chevron Corp owns 50 percent in TengizChevroil (TCO), the $20-billion venture to exploit reserves in western Kazakhstan, with fellow American oil major Mobil Corp and the Kazakh government each owning 25 percent.
Alekperov said the terms of LUKoil's contract to buy five percent of Chevron's share in Tengiz were being agreed.
"The talks are not about the price of our stake, they are about the payment of our stake in tranches, that is to say over what period we will pay the money. We have agreed the price," Alekperov said.
He added that LUKoil expected to conclude the terms of the purchase by early February.

Alekperov said LUKoil and Chevron officials met on January 14 in Moscow and discussed the possibility of making the payment of the three tranches dependent on the progress of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) project.
"Tengiz depends on the CPC," Alekpetrov said.

The CPC consortium, which is to build a pipeline from the oil reserves in western Kazakhstan to Black Sea ports, comprises three country participants -- Kazakhstan (19 percent), Russia (24 pct) and Oman (seven pct) -- and eight companies -- Chevron Corp (15 pct), Mobil (7.5 pct), Orix (1.75 pct), British Gas plc (2 pct), Agip SpA (2 pct), LUKoil and ARCO (12.5 pct), Rossneft and Shell (7.5 pct) and the Kazakh state firm Munaigas (1.75 pct).
He also said the next step for LUKoil was to consider buying into Kazkhstan's stake.
"This will form the next stage of the talks. But we have made an official proposal (to Kazakhstan)," Alekperov said.
